name: Deadlock
notes: Named as a Steam game without a profile is, so that its logs and its Windows environment stay where they were before it had one. Source 2, Direct3D 11. On a MacBook Air M3 (1920x1243 points) the game's borderless window at the display's size ran its title screen at 75 frames a second with 23 ms from a frame's start to the end of its GPU work. The game renders 720 lines whatever screen it is shown and upscales to the screen's size, and what it does at the screen's size is most of a frame: a 1440x932 screen ran at 90, a 1280x829 one at 93, a 1098x711 one (which it renders as it is) at 97 to 100 with 17 ms, a 1024x663 one at 104 to 107 with 16 ms and blocky text (docs/perf/latency.md, 'Deadlock on the M3'). renderPixels is the 1098x711 one: on the chips with the base GPU the game is shown a screen of about that many pixels and the picture is scaled up to fill the display (Wine patch 0017). A player whose settings were made at the display's size keeps the render scale they had there (0.58 of the screen it is shown), which is fewer pixels than before: the game's Render Quality setting puts it back. In the game's practice map the same screen ran at 70 while the Mac was cool. Measured on the M3 only; the M1 and M2 have a slower GPU and the M4's is about a fifth faster. The Pro and Max chips are left at the display's size, unmeasured.
